# Surgery Field medicine keeps people fighting. Surgery finishes the job. The medigun and bone stapler only patch a casualty up part of the way. A doctor at a table fixes what they leave behind.
## When someone needs surgery - A [color=#a4885c]broken bone[/color]. A broken arm makes shots and swings fumble, and a broken leg slows the patient down. - A [color=#a4885c]severed limb[/color] that needs to go back on. - [color=#a4885c]Organ damage[/color], which stops the part healing. - Deep [color=#a4885c]bleeding[/color] or wounds that bandages can't close.
## Starting 1. Get the patient lying down. An operating table or a field hospital is best.
2. Use a surgical tool on the patient. If the tool fits the next step, that step starts. If not, the surgery window opens. You can also right-click the patient and pick [color=#a4885c]Start surgery[/color].
3. The window opens on the part that needs help most. Click another part on the doll to switch. Hurt parts are coloured, and a missing part takes you to the part it goes back on.
4. Follow the plan on the right. Press [color=#a4885c]Perform[/color] to do the step marked ▶, or click a step marked • to do that one.
## Reading the plan The plan lists everything wrong with the part in the order to fix it: opening it up, each problem, then closing it up. - ✓ is done, ▶ is next, • can be done now, and · has to wait for something earlier. - A problem that has to wait says why, like bleeding that has to stop before the bones can be mended. - When a step can't start, the reason is written under it. - Each step names the tool it will use, where that tool is and how long it takes. - Problems you fix stay on the list, marked fixed.
You don't need the tool in your hand. Tools in your hands, your bag or on the floor next to you are found automatically.
## Working faster - [color=#a4885c]Do all[/color] starts each next step by itself until the part is fixed and closed. Moving away, a missing tool or an interrupted step stops it. - Using a tool on the patient outside combat mode does the next step that tool fits, starting with the part you are aiming at. - Medical staff operate four times faster and can work through clothing. Anyone else has to take off the clothing covering the part first.
## Other procedures Amputation, transplants and implants are under [color=#a4885c]Other procedures[/color] at the bottom of the plan. None of them treat an injury, so the plan never suggests them. Pick one to see its steps, and press [color=#a4885c]Back to plan[/color] to return.
## Pay Every problem you fix pays, up to three per patient each wave. Like kill pay, it goes up on later waves. Opening and closing a part pays nothing by itself.
## Tools
Surgery crates and duffels hold a full set. The medical techfab prints every tool, including bone gel and stitches. In a pinch, any sharp item works as a slow scalpel or saw.
## Doing it safely - Wear [color=#a4885c]gloves and a mask[/color]. Without them, every step gives the patient a dose of toxin. - A sleeping patient feels far less pain. Nitrous oxide works well.
## In the field The bone stapler mends broken bones a little at a time, and the medigun heals most of the way. Both stop short of a full repair, so send the patient to a doctor afterwards.
